definition: Segmenting cell nuclei across multiple tissue types in histopathology images — a benchmark for generalizable biomedical segmentation.
details: Segmenting cell nuclei across multiple tissue types in histopathology images — a benchmark for generalizable biomedical segmentation.

explainer.lead: Multi-tissue nucleus segmentation segments cell nuclei across multiple tissue types in histopathology images. It serves as a benchmark for generalizable biomedical segmentation.

tiers.eli5: Finding and outlining every cell's center dot in microscope pictures taken from many different kinds of tissue.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to test whether a segmentation model generalizes across tissue types rather than overfitting to one. The pitfall is that performance on one tissue may not transfer to others.
tiers.paperLevel: The task is segmenting cell nuclei across multiple tissue types in histopathology images, used as a benchmark for generalizable biomedical segmentation.

explainer.example: A model trained and evaluated on histopathology images spanning several tissue types, scored on how well its nucleus outlines hold up across them.
